question.text: A telegraph line of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> has a capacity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>km</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and it carries an alternating current at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> kilo cycle per second. If minimum impedance is required, then the value of the inductance that needs to be introduced in series is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mH</mi></math>. (If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>10</mn></msqrt></math>)

solution.text:
The frequency given is 0.5 kilo cycle per second ⇒f=500 Hz⇒ω=2πf=1000π rad s-1.

Total capacitance of the wire is C=0.01×10-6×100 F.

Impedance is minimum at resonance. Therefore, for minimum impedance

XL=XC

⇒ωL=1ωC⇒L=1ω2C=110002×π2×0.01×10-6×100=10-1 H=100 mH
